title: Wiley College scholarship and the order of his early bands
summary: Tate went to Wiley College on a music scholarship; Giddins sorts out the sequence of his early big bands.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers

blocks.x: Was your schooling at all interrupted by all that touring with the band?

Yeah, I did. You see, I finished. Then I didn't go to college until maybe after I'd been playing with Holder. You know, I didn't until I got a chance to -- I was playing with Holder. So when they said they'd give me a scholarship in music if I would come down and play with the band. So when I went -- that's when I went, like around 1930 -- after leaving Andy Kirk. See, I joined Andy Kirk and I went -- I says, "I think I'm going to take this up and go back home." So we went there and that's the band that Nat Toles took over, the---all of the band from the school. Nat Toles became the leader of that band and I stayed with that band. That was the band we had --
That was Wylie College in Marshall, Texas. So I just went there and studied music and I got a anything else I want to break, you know, anything else. That's the only --/study I could.
Before you went to college though, you were playing with Troy Floyd, 1930.
And you're 15 and then you went to T. Holder's Clouds of Joy.
And so tell me about how you got to T. Holder's (inaudible).
Well, T. Holder -- I went to T. Holder before Troy Floyd, actually.
And actually, that was the first big band. So, well, see, after T. Holder lost this -- after they gave this band to Andy Kirk, --
